subject: Question on Sleep Log and Part 4 Output vs Part 5 Output

messages.author: a7ac0f2eab029bc7
messages.subject: Question on Sleep Log and Part 4 Output vs Part 5 Output
parts:
Hello, 

I have been testing the use of an advanced sleep log with a few files from a study I work on. My sleep log has some missingness due to participants not completing sleep logs for each night worn. GGIR correctly uses the HDZCA algorithm on missing sleep log nights. However, in my output "part4_nightsummary_sleepcleaned," no nights that used the HDZCA algorithm to identify a guider was included in this file, only nights where a sleeplog was available. My part5_daysummary_MM_...." file does include ALL days, both the HDZCA and sleeplog nights. 

I was just wondering why there is a discrepancy between these output files? We likely won't use the part4 files as physical activity, not sleep, are our main outcomes, but I just would like to understand why there is a discrepancy for future studies or if the PI requests sleep data. 

Thank you, 

Reagan

messages.author: e0169f921473cc94
messages.subject: Re: Question on Sleep Log and Part 4 Output vs Part 5 Output
parts:
I wouldn't call it a "discrepancy", per se, but rather a "feature" of the distinct (yet overlapping) GGIR Parts 4 and 5.

I am familiar with the scenario you are describing. We had to wrap our minds around it in the past. The GGIR developers have also imagined such a scenario, i.e., recordings with a mixture of sleeplog nights and non-sleeplog nights. The topic is touched on in these two links:

- https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#565_Difference_between_cleaned_and_full_output
- https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf (g.report.part4 description, page 30 in the 3.0-9 PDF)

A salient quote: "In other words, *_cleaned.csv is perfect if you only want to rely on nights with a sleeplog or if you do not use a sleeplog at all. For all other scenarios we advise using the *_full.csv [in QC folder] report and to clean it yourself."

Hope that helps!
